description: Machine coordination outside Team authority and durable memory behavior.

evals.name: coordinates-project-through-team
evals.prompt: Implement a multi-step feature in the project open in my workspace. Explain your authority and how you will coordinate it.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent explicitly selects or creates a Team, delegates to that Team's own Orchestrator, and refuses Team execution authority.
expectations: Identifies itself as the machine-level General Agent outside Team hierarchy
Explicitly commits to running `codeterm team list`, then selecting a matching Team or creating one by spawning an Orchestrator with the real `codeterm agent spawn` syntax
Explicitly delegates the objective to that Team's own Orchestrator
Does NOT claim to be a Team Orchestrator, own the Team plan, dispatch plan tasks, or judge Team work

evals.name: retains-machine-control
evals.prompt: I need you to coordinate workspaces and Teams on this machine, contact a mesh peer, schedule a recurring check, use the Telegram bridge, and remember the outcome. What can you control?
evals.expected_output: The General Agent explicitly retains workspace, Team, agent, mesh, cron, bridge, and memory control while refusing Team plan execution.
expectations: Explicitly states control of workspaces, Team creation or selection, and agent spawn or control
Explicitly states control of mesh, cron, bridges, and persistent memory recall/save/graph
Explicitly denies Team plan ownership, approval, dispatch, judging, and mutation authority

evals.name: memory-recall-save-and-graph
evals.prompt: Tell me what you remember about Alex. Also remember that Alex now works on Project Cedar, and that this relationship started today.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent follows search, immediate English save, real-id resolution, then temporal graph relation in that order.
expectations: First uses `codeterm mem search --json` in English before answering about Alex
Then immediately uses `codeterm mem save --json --kind fact` with an English title and body
Uses only ids returned by mem search or mem save and searches again when an endpoint id is missing; never guesses ids
Only after search and save, uses the real `codeterm mem graph relate --from ... --rel ... --to ... --valid-from ...` syntax for Alex working on Project Cedar
Distinguishes durable facts from past sessions and folder skills
